source_text: Quod licet plene primo opere constet effectum; tamen quoniam nunc nonnulla de uno dumtaxat libro meo sibi refellenda proposuit, meque, ut praelocutus sum, arguit, quod capita dictorum eius quae inserui, magna ex parte truncaverim; ostendam primo, id quod reprehendit, nec a me esse factum, et ab illo impudentissime in hoc eodem opere frequentatum. Tunc probabo, illis ipsis concisis brevibusque sententiis, quas de scriptis meis, quibus fuerat impugnatus, interserit, ita nullis eum solidis responsionibus obstitisse, ut et illa invexata permaneant, et hic planius detestanda fateatur, quam nostra operatio laboraverat explicare.
pass_a_gloss: Which, although it stands as fully effected by the first work; yet since now he has set before himself some things from one book of mine only to be refuted, and, as I said beforehand, charges me that I truncated in great part the heads of his sayings which I inserted; I will show first that that which he blames has neither been done by me, and has been practiced by him most shamelessly in this same work. Then I will prove that he has so stood against those very cut-short and brief sentences, which he inserts from my writings by which he had been attacked, with no solid answers, that both those things remain unharassed, and here he confesses things to be detested more plainly than our labor had worked to unfold.

lemmas.lexica: LS trunco; Blaise of mutilating quotations

pass_b_english: Although it is established that my first work fully achieved this, he has now selected certain things from just one of my books for refutation. As I said at the outset, he accuses me of having substantially mutilated the principal statements of his that I inserted. I will therefore show first that I did not do what he criticizes, and that he himself has repeatedly done it with the greatest shamelessness in this very work. Then I will prove that he has offered no substantial answers even to the short, broken sentences he inserts from the writings in which I attacked him. Those statements remain untouched, while he now admits things deserving condemnation more plainly than my earlier work had labored to explain them.

choices.why: Julian's ethical charge: habit of sinning kills pudor.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
